subject: Post-call: Reliability priorities and fallback options — FinOptic
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finoptic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Reliability priorities and fallback options — FinOptic

Thanks again for your time today, Samantha — good conversation. Below is a concise recap so we’re aligned on the reliability requirements, current environment, and clear next steps. Please call out anything I missed.

High-level summary (what we heard)
- Primary concern: recent multi-hour outage during peak accounting close window (Feb 12) where model endpoints in eu-west experienced capacity thrash and requests timed out. Business impact: delayed report generation for 2 business days and manual workarounds.
- Pain points: inconsistent p99 latency spikes, lack of automatic graceful-degradation, and limited visibility into per-customer token costs during incidents.
- Current stack: on-prem GPU cluster (mixed A100 and V100), regional failover to a single cloud region (us-east), internal caching but no cross-region KV cache, model variants: large-llm-v1 and a smaller distilled-v1 for cost backups.

Success criteria (what FinOptic needs from a pilot)
1) Availability SLA target: >= 99.95% for customer-facing endpoints during business hours.
2) Latency SLO: p99 < 250ms on typical doc sizes; clear alerting at 150ms deviation.
3) Graceful degradation: automatic fallback to a cheaper/quantized model or alternate region with preserved response shape and compatible API.
4) Observability: token-level billing visibility and per-route traces during incidents.

Proposed technical mitigations we discussed
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat requests and session-level caching to reduce token compute.
- Multi-variant routing: route to distilled-v1 automatically if p99 exceeds threshold, with a short TTL-based rollback when health recovers.
- Cross-region routing and warm standbys for busy windows (we discussed us-east warm capacity tied to peak windows).

Attachments included: consolidated incident summary (reliability_qa.pdf) and a first-pass arch diagram (redwood_arch_diagram.png).

Next steps (agreed on call)
- Connor: share mutual action plan draft + SOC2 summary and an updated arch showing warm standbys (by Mon 3/9) [attachment: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx].
- Samantha: confirm internal stakeholders for procurement and security (you mentioned Luis and procurement@finoptic.com).
- Schedule: agree pilot scope (2 endpoints, 2-week smoke test, metrics: availability/latency & cost delta).

Questions for you to confirm
1) Is the availability target of 99.95% sufficient or do you need 99.99% for these endpoints?
2) Any regulatory constraints around cross-region data movement for customer PII?

Thanks — I’ll follow up Monday with the M.A.P and SOC2 summary.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
[attachment: reliability_qa.pdf (PDF)] [attachment: redwood_arch_diagram.png (PNG)]

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finoptic.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luis Garcia <luis@finoptic.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finoptic.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Reliability priorities and fallback options — FinOptic

Connor — thanks for the clear recap and for capturing the incident detail. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Availability: 99.95% during business hours is our target for MVP endpoints. We will require 99.99% for any financial-reporting SLA in production, but the pilot can aim for 99.95% to validate approach.
- Data residency: PII must remain in-region for EU customers. For US endpoints we can use cross-region warm-standby, but for EU traffic we need a local fallback model instance (no cross-region movement of raw PII).
- Graceful degradation: preserving response format is critical — we can accept small quality delta but not structural changes.

Action items from us: Luis will coordinate security questionnaire and will review your SOC2 summary. Procurement is copied for contract cadence and will send our standard MSA redlines once we see pricing for the pilot.

I’m attaching the Feb incident postmortem excerpt internally — I redacted a few items but it gives color on the demand spike pattern.

Thanks — let’s set a 30-minute slot on Wednesday to walk the MAP and stack diagram.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform Reliability, FinOptic
[attachment: finoptic_feb_postmortem_excerpt.pdf (PDF)]

Date: 2026-03-10T11:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Reliability priorities and fallback options — FinOptic

Connor/Avery — I sketched a first-pass mutual action plan and added a short checklist for the pilot. Highlights:
- Pilot scope: 2 endpoints (report-generation, reconciliation-assist), 14 days smoke + 30 days observational.
- Success gates: 99.95% availability during pilot business hours, p99 < 250ms for representative payloads, documented rollback and fallback behavior validated via chaos test.
- Deliverables from Redwood: SOC2 summary, arch diagram with warm-standby notes, a short runbook for failover toggle, and an automated canary that verifies response shape after fallback.

I attached the MAP (mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx) to this thread. Connor — I put placeholder sizing for warm standby and estimated cost uplift; please adjust after you review FinOptic's peak windows.

—Marissa
